item.title: Persuasion and rhetoric
item.description: Words for describing how speakers and writers try to convince an audience.

children.definition: able to express ideas clearly, beautifully and convincingly
children.example: Her eloquent speech persuaded the committee to keep the library open.

children.definition: a question asked for effect, not because an answer is expected
children.example: "Who doesn't want cleaner air?" was clearly a rhetorical question.

children.definition: to influence someone so that they change their opinion
children.example: Undecided voters can be swayed by a single strong debate performance.

children.definition: deliberate exaggeration used for effect, not meant to be taken literally
children.example: Calling the new rule "the end of education" is pure hyperbole.

children.definition: a reply that tries to prove an argument or claim wrong
children.example: Each team has two minutes for its rebuttal.

children.definition: a weaker, distorted version of an opponent's view, set up so it is easy to attack
children.example: Nobody suggested banning cars; that's a straw man.

children.definition: intended to produce strong feelings rather than careful thought
children.example: The article used emotive language to describe the new tax.

children.definition: a way of presenting information so that it gives a favourable impression
children.example: The press release put a positive spin on the disappointing results.

children.definition: a leader who wins support by exploiting people's fears and prejudices rather than by reasoned argument
children.example: History offers many examples of demagogues who promised simple answers to complex problems.

children.definition: using the opinion of a famous or powerful person as proof that a claim is true
children.example: "A celebrity uses this cream" is an appeal to authority, not evidence.

children.definition: a short, memorable phrase from a speech, chosen to be repeated in the media
children.example: Politicians often prepare a sound bite before an interview.

children.definition: to try to persuade people who already agree with you
children.example: Posting only in our own group is just preaching to the converted.
